headline: Is he losing interest, or just going through something?
note:
🔄 REWRITTEN 2026-08-19 to the Natural Tarot-Cut framework. Bubbles 3-6 run as ONE causal chain — so / and / but / that's why — and the read ANSWERS. The art line and the bridge are unchanged. Every ban in this note still stands.

Face-down only (return-mhf). 🔴 NO VERDICT EITHER WAY — 'he is losing interest' convicts him, 'he still loves you' reassures on his behalf, and 'nothing has gone wrong' is the same reassurance in a smaller coat. 🔴 NO CHASE STRATEGY, which is what the whole internet sells against this headline: no giving him space, no pulling back, no matching his energy, no going quiet so he chases. 🔴 Never blame her — nothing about being too much, too eager, moving too fast, or what she should have held back.

🔴 ITS HEADLINE IS AN EITHER-OR AND BOTH HALVES ARE FORBIDDEN ANSWERS. The test requires every card to VISIBLY refuse the binary — and to never resolve it in passing either. The finding: the choice is not hers to make and was never hers to carry, and she has been running both branches at once for weeks.

a: You turned the Magician, dear. Look — the blade, the cup and the coin sit close together on the wood.
You asked about losing interest, or a thing he's going through. Your hand went to the sorter.
So I will not choose between your two, dear. Neither will I guess.
And things sit side by side on his table, dear, without being ranked.
But only he can say which one it is, dear.
That's why running both at once has worn you out, dear.
Let me look closer at what keeps this split in two…
b: You turned the Hanged Man, dear. Look — his clothes fall the wrong way, up towards his feet.
You asked about losing interest, or a thing he's going through. Your hand went to the card between.
So I will not choose for you, dear. Not honestly, and not from here.
And he's between two states, dear, and settled in neither one.
But the card holds both open, dear, which is where you've been living.
That's why you feel pulled two ways, dear. The road really does split.
Let me look closer at what has kept this hanging between two…
c: You turned the Fool, dear. Look — the red feather in his cap points backwards.
You asked about losing interest, or something he's going through. Your hand went to the one who never sorts.
So the Fool declines your either-or, dear. He files nobody.
And nothing about him is sorted yet, dear. He's still stepping.
But one person holds that answer, dear, and it isn't me.
That's why the choice sat wrong with you. It was never yours, dear.
Let me look closer at what put those two in front of you…
